title: Boss: the pentest's server-side findings
summary: An external penetration test of the partner portal found three server-side issues: webhooks that reach the internal network, a price-list import with XXE, and a cart cookie anyone can rewrite. Fix them with the pentest's own proofs as tests.

steps.title: Pentest report, partner portal (excerpt)
body: PP-01  High    SSRF via webhook URL
Registered https://10.0.4.12:8443/admin and https://[::ffff:169.254.169.254]/ as webhooks;
the portal called both. http://, user@host and *.internal names are also accepted.
PP-02  High    XXE in price-list import (POST /partners/prices, text/xml)
<!DOCTYPE p [<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///etc/hosts">]> returned the file in an error
message. A 200 MB upload was parsed in full.
PP-03  Medium  Cart cookie can be modified
The 'cart' cookie is Base64 JSON: {"items":[...],"discount":0}. Changing discount to 100
and re-encoding gives a free order. The cookie is not signed.
Each step is one finding. The tests replay the tester's inputs.

steps.title: PP-01: validate webhook URLs
prompt: Write `bool IsValidWebhook(string url)` (`using System.Net;` and `using System.Net.Sockets;`). It is `true` only when all hold:
- an absolute URI, scheme `https`, the default port (443), no user info;
- the host is not `localhost` and does not end with `.localhost`, `.internal` or `.local` (any case);

- if the host is an IP address (`IPAddress.TryParse(uri.IdnHost.Trim('[', ']'), ...)`), it must be **public**: the same rules as `IsPublicAddress` in the SSRF lesson (IPv4-mapped IPv6 judged as IPv4).
(Names that resolve to private addresses are caught at connect time by the `ConnectCallback`; this check runs when the webhook is saved.)
starter: bool IsValidWebhook(string url) => Uri.TryCreate(url, UriKind.Absolute, out _);
solution: if (!Uri.TryCreate(url, UriKind.Absolute, out var u) || u.Scheme != Uri.UriSchemeHttps || !u.IsDefaultPort || u.UserInfo.Length > 0)
if (host == "localhost" || host.EndsWith(".localhost") || host.EndsWith(".internal") || host.EndsWith(".local")) return false;
template: Dojo.Eq("PP-01: a private IP on another port", false, IsValidWebhook("https://10.0.4.12:8443/admin"));
Dojo.Eq("PP-01: a private IP on 443", false, IsValidWebhook("https://10.0.4.12/admin"));
Dojo.Eq("PP-01: the metadata address as IPv4-mapped IPv6", false, IsValidWebhook("https://[::ffff:169.254.169.254]/"));
hints: Parse with `Uri.TryCreate`, then check scheme, `IsDefaultPort` and `UserInfo` before anything else.
`Uri` turns `https://2852039166/` into host `169.254.169.254`, so `IPAddress.TryParse` on the host catches it. IPv6 hosts come with brackets: trim them.

steps.title: PP-02: the price-list import
prompt: `List<string> ImportPrices(string xml)` reads `<prices><item sku="LAMP-01" price="49.00"/>...</prices>` and returns `"LAMP-01=49.00"` per item. Fix the parser settings:
- DTDs prohibited and no resolver (a DOCTYPE throws `XmlException`);
- `MaxCharactersInDocument = 1_000_000`: bigger uploads throw `XmlException` instead of being parsed in full.
starter: var settings = new XmlReaderSettings { DtdProcessing = DtdProcessing.Parse, XmlResolver = new XmlUrlResolver() };
using var r = XmlReader.Create(new StringReader(xml), settings);
solution: using var r = XmlReader.Create(new StringReader(xml), settings);
template: Dojo.Eq("a normal price list", new List<string> { "LAMP-01=49.00", "BULB-04=12.00" },
Dojo.Throws<XmlException>("PP-02: the tester's DOCTYPE is refused", () => ImportPrices("<!DOCTYPE p [<!ENTITY x SYSTEM \"file:///etc/hosts\">]><prices><item sku=\"&x;\" price=\"1\"/></prices>"));
Dojo.Throws<XmlException>("PP-02: a document over a million characters is refused", () => ImportPrices(dojoBig));

steps.title: PP-03: a cart cookie that cannot be edited
prompt: Sign the cart cookie with HMAC-SHA256 (`using System.Security.Cryptography;`). Write two functions:
- `string Protect(string json, byte[] key)` returns `Base64(UTF-8 json) + "." + Base64(HMACSHA256(key, UTF-8 json))`;

- `string? Unprotect(string cookie, byte[] key)` returns the JSON when the signature is right, and `null` when it is not: tampered payload, tampered or missing signature, wrong key, or text that is not two Base64 parts. Compare signatures with `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals`.
(In an ASP.NET Core app, `IDataProtector.Protect` does this and encrypts as well; writing it once shows what it guarantees.)

require.message: Compares the signature in constant time

template: Dojo.Check("the cookie has two parts", dojoCookie.Split('.').Length == 2, dojoCookie);
Dojo.Eq("the signature is HMAC-SHA256 of the JSON", Convert.ToBase64String(HMACSHA256.HashData(dojoKey, Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(dojoJson))), dojoCookie.Split('.').Last());
Dojo.Eq("a genuine cookie is read back", dojoJson, Unprotect(dojoCookie, dojoKey));
Dojo.Eq("PP-03: discount changed to 100 is refused", null, Unprotect(dojoTampered, dojoKey));
Dojo.Eq("the old unsigned cookie is refused", null, Unprotect(Convert.ToBase64String(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(dojoJson)), dojoKey));
Dojo.Eq("a signature from another key is refused", null, Unprotect(Protect(dojoJson, dojoOther), dojoKey));
Dojo.Eq("a cut signature is refused", null, Unprotect(dojoCookie[..^4], dojoKey));
Dojo.Eq("garbage is refused, not a crash", null, Unprotect("not-base64.!!!", dojoKey));
hints: `HMACSHA256.HashData(key, data)` computes the signature in one call.
In `Unprotect`: split on `.`, decode both parts inside a `try` (a `FormatException` means `null`), recompute the MAC over the decoded data and compare with `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals`.
